Purpose: Wave 5 Clinic and EMR shared MySQL migration architecture, security, and migration design validation

NotEvidenced: Approved source MySQL route or VPN
SSM, logging, KMS, or Secrets Manager interface endpoints
Clinic/EMR application, IAM roles, secrets, KMS key, or backup policy

KnownScenario: Clinic Management and EMR share one MySQL datastore and must migrate together.
Doctors, nurses, reception, clinic managers, IT, security, and break-glass roles require distinct application authorization.
PHI, PII, clinical-history integrity, audit continuity, and patient matching are critical.
UnsupportedAssumptions: No commercial Clinic or EMR product, vendor support matrix, source schema, or database inventory was supplied.
MySQL version, size, change rate, topology, storage engines, keys, LOBs, charset, collation, time zone, and application connection behavior are unknown.
Stored procedures, triggers, events, views, grants, partitions, generated columns, and unsupported data types are unknown.
Source route, redundant VPN, DNS, firewall rules, source impact tolerance, and integration contracts are unknown.
RPO 15 minutes, RTO four hours, and 300-second CDC alarm threshold are scenario placeholders, not owner-approved clinical requirements.

Architecture.ApplicationTier: Private EC2, no public IP, no SSH or RDP ingress, IMDSv2, encrypted gp3, Session Manager through external endpoints
Architecture.DatabaseTier: Private Single-AZ RDS MySQL 8.0 design baseline, db.t3.small, encrypted gp3, TLS-required parameter group, automated backups, final snapshot, deletion protection
Architecture.MigrationTier: Private Single-AZ DMS dms.t3.small design using full-load-and-cdc, endpoint TLS verify-full, task validation, bounded logging, and external secrets
Architecture.DatabaseFlow: Application SG and DMS SG to database SG only on TCP/3306
Architecture.SourceFlow: DMS SG to exact private source MySQL CIDRs only on TCP/3306
Architecture.SharedFiles: Existing FSx is optional and external; SMB/445 is modeled only when vendor evidence requires it

RdsDesign.EngineBaseline: MySQL 8.0; source and vendor confirmation required
RdsDesign.Availability: Single-AZ design constraint; not a production recommendation
RdsDesign.Storage: 20 GiB gp3 with 100 GiB ceiling, encrypted using external KMS
RequiresConfirmation: Exact engine version and upgrade path
Instance, IOPS, connection, and storage sizing
Character set, collation, SQL mode, time zone, and parameter compatibility
Audit plugin, protected log destination, and approved retention

DmsDesign.EndpointCredentials: External Secrets Manager ARNs via externally governed exact-purpose role
DmsDesign.EndpointTls: verify-full with externally governed certificate ARNs
DmsDesign.TableMapping: Exact application schema with placeholder all-table selection pending reviewed inventory
DmsDesign.LobMode: Limited LOB mode with conceptual 32 KiB threshold; profiling required and any data or truncation error stops the task
DmsDesign.Logging: Default severity and no intentional row payload, SQL literal, PHI, PII, or secret content
SourcePrerequisites: ROW binary logging and required row image
Adequate binlog retention and unique server ID
Primary or unique keys for reliable CDC
CompatibilityRisks: Procedures, functions, triggers, events, views, users, and grants require separate handling
LOB, data type, collation, time zone, generated-column, and DDL behavior require testing
DMS validation does not replace independent clinical integrity and audit validation

BreakGlassControls: Explicit reason and time-limited minimum scope
Mandatory security and clinical post-use review

ExternalOwnership.SecretRotation: Owner-approved process and rotation evidence required

FsxDesign.DatabaseStores: Structured records and stable file references
FsxDesign.FsxMayStore: Encrypted reports, exports, attachments, or legacy shared files

IntegrityValidationDesign: Row counts by table and clinically meaningful partition
Patient, appointment, encounter, and audit identifier uniqueness
Timestamp, time-zone, precision, and ordering behavior
Encoding, collation, sorting, and equality behavior
RollbackDesign: Preserve state, logs, checkpoints, tests, and decision evidence
Identify and reconcile every target-only or downtime transaction
Return applications to source through reviewed configuration reversal
Revalidate source integrity and authentication before reopening
Choose forward-fix or later retry through change governance

Covers: External FSx only when explicitly selected
BackupRestoreDesign.RestoreValidation: Isolated private restore with integrity, application, RBAC, audit, attachment, and recovery-time checks

KnownWarnings: Sandbox cannot read the user-level Terraform CLI directory; formatting and validation returned exit code 0.
Existing Appointment API DynamoDB hash_key and range_key arguments are deprecated.

BLOCKER: No approved private source route or required interface endpoints are evidenced.
RPO, RTO, acceptable CDC lag, downtime, and clinical continuity decisions are unapproved.
DESIGN REQUIREMENT: Private RDS and DMS with SG-reference-only target access.
Application-layer clinical RBAC and no direct clinical database users.
External least-privilege IAM, secrets, KMS, certificates, and backup ownership.
Verified endpoint TLS, protected minimal logs, independent integrity validation, and explicit break-glass controls.
DESIGN CONSTRAINT: Single-AZ is portfolio sizing, not a production recommendation.
Existing FSx use and compatibility are conditional.
DMS cannot migrate or convert every source object and server setting.
FOLLOW_UP: Profile source database and LOBs, confirm private connectivity, approve clinical recovery and lag thresholds, and define protected audit retention before any implementation design.

CostConsiderations: RDS MySQL runtime, gp3 storage, snapshots, and backups
Temporary DMS replication runtime and storage
KMS operations and AWS Backup retention
Interface endpoints and hybrid data transfer
DMS removal only after separately authorized migration acceptance in a real implementation
